does: Gives a thin hot liquid more body by stirring in a starch, mixed smooth in a little cold liquid first, and bringing it to a simmer so that the starch swells and the liquid turns glossy and coats a spoon.

intro.what: This method thickens hot liquid with starch first dispersed in cold liquid.
intro.why: It teaches you to control lumps and stop before the sauce becomes too stiff on cooling.

how: Mix the starch with a little cold liquid until it is smooth, with no lumps.
Bring the liquid to a gentle simmer and stir it round.
Pour the mixture in a thin stream while stirring, and keep stirring.
Let it bubble gently for a short while so that the raw taste of the starch cooks out and the body is full.
Stop when it coats the back of a spoon. It will thicken a little more as it cools, so take it off the heat while it still pours.

cues.text: The liquid turns glossy and clear, or silky if it holds milk, and coats the back of a spoon.
The spoon drags a little more as it moves through.

mistakes.mistake: Adding the dry starch straight to hot liquid, which lumps.
mistakes.fix: Mix it smooth in cold liquid first.

mistakes.mistake: Boiling hard for long, which breaks the starch down so that the liquid thins again.
mistakes.fix: Let it bubble gently only until it has thickened.

mistakes.mistake: Thickening too much at the start, since it keeps thickening as it cools.
mistakes.fix: Add a little at a time and stop while it still pours.

quiz.question: What happens as dispersed starch heats in the sauce?
choices: It removes all moisture from the pan.
It separates fat into a clear top layer.
It swells and gives the liquid more body.
quiz.because: Swollen starch thickens the surrounding liquid so it can coat a spoon.

quiz.question: How should starch be added to the hot liquid?
choices: As a smooth cold-liquid mixture poured in while stirring.
As a heap of dry powder without stirring.
Scatter dry starch over the hot surface and wait before stirring.
quiz.because: Cold dispersion separates the starch before heat thickens it, reducing lumps.

quiz.question: Which spoon cue indicates added body?
choices: No resistance and no coating at all.
A little more drag and a coating on the back.
Hard dry lumps scraping the base.
quiz.because: A smooth increase in resistance indicates thickening rather than clumping.

quiz.question: The sauce becomes too stiff after cooling. What should change next time?
choices: Keep thickening until it barely moves while hot.
Add all the starch before checking texture.
Add starch gradually and stop while it still pours.
quiz.because: Cooling can increase the apparent thickness, so the hot sauce should retain flow.

comes_after.why: Starch thickens at a simmer, so a cook has to be able to hold a liquid there.
